title: Protecting Routes with Middleware
description: Combine NextAuth and Edge Middleware to guard pages and redirect unauthenticated users.

slides.title: The Guard at the Edge 🛡️
slides.content:
# Middleware + NextAuth

We previously wrote middleware to check for a cookie. With NextAuth, we can use its built‑in `getToken` helper to verify the JWT from the request.

Alternatively, NextAuth provides a dedicated middleware function `withAuth` that wraps our middleware or can be used directly.

This runs at the edge, so redirections happen before the page even loads.

slides.title: Using next-auth/middleware (middleware.js)
slides.content: Export a default middleware using `withAuth`. It automatically redirects unauthenticated users to the sign‑in page.

quizData.question: What does exporting `{ default } from 'next-auth/middleware'` do?

options.text: It adds authentication to all API routes
It creates a middleware that checks for a valid NextAuth session and redirects if missing
It disables middleware for auth routes

quizData.explanation: `next-auth/middleware` exports a function that wraps the default middleware, adding session verification. It's the fastest way to protect pages.

slides.title: Custom Middleware with getToken 🛠️
Role‑Based Middleware (middleware.js)
slides.content: Only allow users with an 'admin' role to access /admin.

quizData.question: When would you use `getToken` instead of the `withAuth` middleware?

options.text: When you need to check for authentication only
When you need access to the full token payload (e.g., roles) and custom redirect logic
When you want to bypass authentication

quizData.explanation: `getToken` returns the decoded JWT with any custom data you stored, enabling fine‑grained access control.
